title: Hosted Endpoint Compatibility, Degradation Contracts, and Launch Checklist
creator: Asha Patel
description: PRD that defines compatibility guarantees and formal degradation/fallback contracts for hosted inference endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Purpose: provide deterministic behavior when capacity, model variants, or regional failures trigger graceful degradation, and codify acceptance criteria and launch checklist for the hosted product team.
goals: Define compatibility matrix for client API surface across model variants and fallbacks
Specify concrete degradation semantics for latency-first and cost-first policies
Establish acceptance criteria and pre-launch validations for SLOs, fallbacks, and audits
Provide rollout checklist and monitoring alerts to detect regression in quality or availability
non_goals: Design new SDK surface changes (SDK teams will implement compatible client adapters separately)
Implement on-prem/private deployment changes (this PRD is scoped to hosted endpoints only)
Rewrite model routing engine — only configuration and contract changes are in scope
requirements: Compatibility: Requests using existing API fields (messages, prompt, functions, user_metadata) must behave identically for primary model and any in-family fallback for 95% of documented call patterns
Degradation policies: The system must expose two vendor-facing policies: latency-first and cost-first, each with deterministic fallback behavior documented in the SDK contract
Fallback determinism: When a primary model is downgraded, the platform must return a header 'x-rw-fallback' with model-id and reason code

Quality guardrails: For any fallback that changes model family (e.g., LLM-4 -> LLM-3-compatible), system must run a quick eval on a seeded prompt set and surface a regression score before routing 100% traffic
Regional fallback: Automatic cross-region fallback must be opt-in per customer, with clear data residency implications recorded in the audit log
API invariants: Endpoint response schema (status codes, error payload shapes, streaming event types) must remain stable across rollouts
Telemetry: Per-request metadata (latency, model_latency, tokens_in, tokens_out, fallback_reason) must be emitted to the console and exported to metrics stream
SLOs: 99th percentile P99 latency for text-generation endpoints must be <= 750ms for non-streaming flows under target load in smoke tests
Security: Fallbacks cannot route to models flagged for data retention differences unless key-manager policy explicitly allows it
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix coverage report completed and reviewed by SDK and infra teams
Automated regression eval shows <3% drop in quality for any candidate fallback on the canonical seed set
End-to-end smoke tests pass in three regions (us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast) including simulated model failover
Console shows fallback audit trail and per-route fallback rates under the new rollout for 48 hours without customer-facing errors
Release notes drafted with explicit migration guidance and opt-in flags for cross-region fallback
Security review signed off and KMS routing policy updated if any fallback requires different key usage
Observability alerts created: 'fallback-rate > 5% over 15m', 'quality_regression > 3% on eval set', and 'model-unavailable-rate > 1%'
scope_changes: 2025-02-18: Removed proposed automatic cross-customer rollback behavior — decision to use canary + manual rollback instead (see Decisions)
2025-02-24: Narrowed non-goal to exclude SDK surface changes after discussion with DX; added requirement for header-level fallback determinism
2025-02-28: Added explicit quality guardrail eval requirement after infra raised rollback risk
rollout_checklist: Finalize compatibility matrix and publish to shared Confluence (PM, SDK, Infra signatures)
Create canary in us-west with 2% traffic using 'latency-first' policy for 24h
Run seeded regression eval six times during canary window and compare to baseline
Instrument header 'x-rw-fallback' and verify presence in sample traces
Enable fallback audit logs to S3 with encryption and retention policy set per compliance
Coordinate with Support and Solutions to prepare customer comms and migration guide
Open GitHub release PR for hosted-api-2025.03 and link necessary infra migration changes
Run chaos test: simulate model worker OOM and verify deterministic fallback behavior
Promote to 20% traffic and monitor alerts for 72h before full rollout
Post-launch: 7-day smoke dashboard and quality review with Research/Applied ML
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics: fallback_rate, fallback_by_model, p99_latency_by_endpoint, quality_eval_score, model_unavailable_count
Alert: fallback-rate > 5% sustained for 15m -> page SRE and PM
Alert: quality_eval_score delta > 3% -> notify Research and PM slack channel #product-quality
Dashboard: Per-route waterfall including time-in-queue, model_latency, tokens_in/out
Tracing: Ensure fallback header is captured in 100% of sampled traces
migration_strategy: Opt-in cross-region fallback disabled by default; customers can enable via tenant flag and acknowledge residency implications
Customers with pinned model versions are excluded from automatic fallback; they receive 503 and a migration recommendation
Provide a migration runbook: steps to opt into fallback, how to pin model variants, and rollback steps
Offer a limited migration assistance program for enterprise customers during first 12 weeks post-launch
compatibility_matrix_summary: Primary matrix maps API fields and behaviors across model families and fallback classes; full matrix stored in Confluence link below.
decisions: Use deterministic fallback header 'x-rw-fallback' rather than modifying response body to preserve client parsing stability (2025-02-14)
Canary approach adopted; full auto-rollback removed in favor of manual rollback with automated signals (2025-02-18)
Seeded regression eval will be single-turn canonical prompts owned by Research and restricted to 100 items to keep runtime affordable (2025-02-28)
open_questions: Should we version the fallback header schema (x-rw-fallback-v) from day one? Trade-off: future proof vs. client complexity
What is acceptable fallback latency delta per customer tier before we force a circuit-break (P0 customers may expect stricter limits)
Do we expose a lightweight API to let customers opt into quality-only fallbacks (i.e., prefer higher-quality slower model rather than latency-first)?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Fallback causes silent quality regressions for non-seeded prompts. Mitigation: sampling-based human review for top 0.1% traffic and automated evals
Risk: Customers misconfigure cross-region fallback violating residency. Mitigation: require explicit tenant acknowledgement and audit log entry before enabling
Risk: Increased token cost when falling back to larger models under cost-first policy during transient events. Mitigation: cost budget throttles and per-tenant circuit-breaker
